item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:

What is the measure of angle C in the triangle above?
item.figure_description: A right triangle ABC with the right angle at vertex A in the lower left, marked with a square symbol. The vertical side AB goes up to vertex B at the top, where the angle is marked with an arc and labeled 35°. The horizontal side AC extends to the right to vertex C, where an arc marks the interior angle.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A large triangle. The left angle is 45 degrees and the top angle is 65 degrees. A line is drawn on the side between the 45 and 64 degree angle to form two smaller triangles—one adjacent to the larger triangle, and one contained within the larger triangle. The right most angle of the triangle adjacent to the larger triangle has an angle of 30 degrees. The smaller triangle contained within the bigger triangle has an angle x that is formed by the right side of the triangle and the drawn line.]

In the figure above, what is the value of x?
reference_items.figure_description: A geometric figure featuring intersecting lines and triangles. A triangle has a horizontal base, a left side with an interior angle of 45° at the bottom-left vertex, and an interior angle of 65° at the top vertex. A line segment extends from the top vertex down to the base. A second line segment extends from a point on the left side of the triangle down and to the right, crossing the first line segment and ending at the rightmost endpoint of the extended horizontal base, where the interior angle is labeled 30°. Near the top vertex, a smaller triangle is bounded by the upper part of the left side, the upper part of the segment from the top vertex, and the crossing segment; the interior angle at the intersection of the two segments is marked with an arc and labeled x.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Geometric figure with parallel lines and triangle]

In this figure, line l is parallel to line m. The measure of angle DAC is 55°.
What is the value of x + y?
reference_items.figure_description: Two horizontal parallel lines are shown: line l on top and line m on the bottom. Points A and D lie on line l, with D to the right of A. Points B and C lie on line m, with C to the right of B. Line segments AB and AC connect the two lines, forming triangle ABC. A dashed arc indicates that angle DAC measures 55°. Inside triangle ABC, angle BAC at vertex A is marked with an arc labeled x°, and angle ABC at vertex B is marked with a dashed arc labeled y°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
In this figure, triangles ABC and DEF are congruent with BC = EF .

[Image: Overlapping triangles ABC and DEF]

What is the measure of angle EGC ?
reference_items.figure_description: Two overlapping triangles, ABC and DEF, resting on a shared horizontal baseline containing points B, E, C, and F in that order from left to right. Segment BC is the base of triangle ABC, and segment EF is the base of triangle DEF. Vertex A is above the baseline, and vertex D is to the right of A and also above the baseline. Side AC intersects side DE at point G. Angle B is labeled 40°, and angle F is labeled 60°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Two triangles]

The triangles shown are congruent. The measures of some of the sides and angles are given. What is the value of x?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two triangles are shown side by side.
The left triangle has a horizontal bottom side. Its left side is labeled "6 cm". The interior angle at the bottom-left vertex is labeled "49°", and the interior angle at the top vertex is labeled "81°".
The right triangle has a nearly horizontal bottom side that slopes slightly downward from right to left, labeled "6 cm". The interior angle at the bottom-right vertex is labeled "81°", and the interior angle at the top vertex is labeled "x°".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Geometric diagram]

In this diagram, CD = CE.
What is the value of x?
reference_items.figure_description:
A geometric diagram with two triangles, ABC and CDE, meeting at vertex C.
- Segment BD is a horizontal line containing point C between B and D.
- Segment AE is a straight line that intersects line BD at point C.
- Segment AB is vertical and perpendicular to BD, with a right-angle square mark shown at angle ABC.
- Line segment AB extends slightly above point A.
- Angle BAC is marked with an arc and labeled 50°.
- On triangle CDE, segment CD and segment CE each have a single tick mark indicating CD = CE.
- Segment DE connects points D and E.
- Angle CDE at vertex D is marked with an arc.
- Angle DEC at vertex E is marked with an arc and labeled x°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Which angle in the figure has a measure closest to 45°?

[Image: Circle divided into angles p, q, r, and s]
reference_items.figure_description: A circle contains a vertical diameter dividing it into left and right halves. From the center, two additional line segments (radii) are drawn: one extending to the left edge at roughly 9 o'clock (slightly below horizontal), and another extending down and to the right at approximately a 45-degree angle from the vertical. Four central angles are labeled: angle q is in the upper-left quadrant (between the upward vertical radius and the left radius, roughly 90°); angle p is in the lower-left quadrant (between the left radius and the downward vertical radius, roughly 90°); angle r is in the upper-right (between the upward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, an obtuse angle of roughly 135°); and angle s is in the lower-right (between the downward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, roughly 45°).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Regular hexagon PQRSTU]

PQRSTU is a regular hexagon. What is the measure of the angle QUS?
reference_items.figure_description: A regular hexagon with vertices labeled clockwise: P at the top left, Q at the top right, R at the far right, S at the bottom right, T at the bottom left, and U at the far left. Segment PQ forms the top horizontal edge, and segment TS forms the bottom horizontal edge. Two internal straight line segments are drawn: one connecting vertex U to vertex Q, and another connecting vertex U to vertex S, forming angle QUS.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
